note: The comparison against the underwritten base case, by hand (docs/08 section 11, rules 4 to 6), with tolerances of 5% on plan and 2 points of IRR. The company is the worked example of section 8: entry snapshot 2021-06-30 with revenue 200,000,000, EBITDA 40,000,000, EV 400,000,000 (10.0x) and net debt 150,000,000. Case 1, worked example 2: planned exit 2026-06-30 at 11.0x with EBITDA 80,000,000 and net debt 100,000,000, so EV 880,000,000; planned EBITDA growth (80 - 40) x 10.0 = 400,000,000, multiple expansion (880 - 400) - 400 = 80,000,000, debt paydown 50,000,000, total 530,000,000; the actual bridge at 2024-06-30 is 250,000,000, 65,000,000 and 30,000,000, total 345,000,000; progress 0.625, 0.8125, 0.6 and 345 / 530 = 0.6509433962; 1,096 of 1,826 days, 0.6002190581. The quarter of 2024-06-30 lies 366 of 1,096 days between the plan dates 2023-06-30 and 2026-06-30: EBITDA 56,000,000 + 24,000,000 x 366 / 1,096 = 64,014,598.5401459854, revenue 250,000,000 + 70,000,000 x 366 / 1,096 = 273,375,912.4087591241, net debt 130,000,000 - 30,000,000 x 366 / 1,096 = 119,981,751.8248175182. The series holds the three plan dates and the approved quarters up to the current one; the quarter of 2024-09-30 is dated after it and is left out. We invested 10,000,000 on 2021-06-30, received 2,000,000 on 2023-06-30 and hold a NAV of 22,500,000: MOIC 2.45; the path value at 20% is 10,000,000 x 1.2^(1096/365) - 2,000,000 x 1.2^(366/365). Case 2, worked example 3, as of 2023-06-30 on a plan date: 10,000,000 in, 1,000,000 back 730 days on and a NAV of 12,000,000; MOIC 1.3, IRR sqrt(1.3) - 1 = 0.1401754251, gap -0.0598245749, behind; path value 10,000,000 x 1.44 - 1,000,000 = 13,400,000, path MOIC 1.44, gap -0.14. The actual bridge with an EV of 580,000,000 is (55 - 40) x 10 = 150,000,000, (580 - 400) - 150 = 30,000,000 and 20,000,000, total 200,000,000: progress 0.375, 0.375, 0.4 and 200 / 530 = 0.3773584906; 730 of 1,826 days. Cases 3 and 4, worked example 4: a loan of 10,000,000 at par on 2021-06-30 paying 1,000,000 on each anniversary, underwritten at 10%, as of 2023-06-30. At par the IRR is 10%, on plan, and the path value 12,100,000 - 1,100,000 - 1,000,000 = 10,000,000, path MOIC 1.2, gap 0. Marked at 9,000,000 the MOIC is 1.1, the gap -0.1 and the IRR 0.0512492197 (10x^2 - x - 10 = 0), 0.0487507803 under: behind. A loan carries its returns and its yield to maturity as given, and nothing else. Case 5: a plan whose net debt rises to 160,000,000 plans a debt paydown of -10,000,000, so that driver has no progress; an actual multiple expansion of -40,000,000 against a planned 80,000,000 is -0.5; total 240 / 470 = 0.5106382979. Case 6: an exit at the entry multiple and the entry net debt plans exactly 0 for both, so neither has progress; total 240 / 400 = 0.6. With no Locked valuation there is no MOIC and no IRR, so no gap; the path still stands. Case 7: a plan that ended on 2023-12-31 (10.5x, EBITDA 62,000,000, net debt 125,000,000: planned 220,000,000, 31,000,000 and 25,000,000, total 276,000,000) read on 2024-06-30: no plan figure for the quarter and no path; progress 250 / 220, 65 / 31, 30 / 25 and 345 / 276 = 1.25, with 1,096 of 914 days passed. Case 8: realized on 2023-12-31 for 24,000,000 after 2,000,000 earlier: MOIC 2.6 against an underwritten 2.5 at exit, a gap of 0.1; no path and no reason. Its current quarter is the one at its exit. Case 9: no entry snapshot, so no bridge either way and no time passed; the quarter is still set against plan. Case 10: the plan point on the planned exit has no net debt, so there is no planned bridge; the actual one stands. Case 11: as of 2021-09-30 there is no approved quarter and nothing has been invested: no metrics, the series holds the plan dates alone, the planned bridge stands and there is no path. Case 12: an EBITDA of zero at the planned exit has no multiple, so no planned bridge. The gross IRR of cases 1, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 12 (0.360867922) and of case 8 (0.4742687072) are inputs, solved by bisection at 60 digits; every other figure is plain arithmetic.
